question: does a multi-PC image block work better than the single lag -- and does it fix the singleton objection?
construction: per-fetus mean USFM emb_l5 over that fetus's IMPACT frames (918 fetuses, 94.0% coverage), PCA to 5 components (89.1% of embedding variance; PC1 alone 71.1%)

finding_1_the_singleton_fix_FAILS.reading: THE PREMISE OF THIS EXPERIMENT IS WRONG. Within-block R2 for the image PCs is -0.007 -- every PC is at or below zero. PCA components are ORTHOGONAL BY CONSTRUCTION, so a PC block has no within-block redundancy to reconstruct from, by definition. It looks like a 5-variable block but behaves as five singletons. The tabular blocks reach 0.508. This does NOT fix the objection the agent raised about the single lag; it reproduces it five times.

finding_2_cross_block_rises.reading: image-PC cross-block R2 is 0.058, ABOVE the tabular 0.039 -- the first image representation to exceed the tabular budget. Driven almost entirely by PC3 at 0.129.

finding_3_what_PC3_actually_is.reading: PC3 IS MATERNAL HABITUS, NOT FETAL PHYSIOLOGY. It correlates 0.34 with maternal BMI and 0.32 with maternal weight -- higher BMI degrades ultrasound image quality (attenuation, depth), so the encoder is reading acquisition conditions. Its correlation with the maturation lag is only 0.11. The 'gain' in cross-block R2 is the image block predicting how heavy the mother is.

finding_4_acquisition_artefact.reading: PC4 correlates 0.34 with the NUMBER of images acquired for that fetus -- another acquisition artefact, not biology

factor_structure.reading: PC3 reaches loading 0.35, the others 0.10-0.14. So an image PC DOES enter the latent -- but it is the maternal-habitus one.

VERDICT: Worse than the lag, not better. The multi-PC block fails on its own motivation (PCs cannot have within-block structure), and the extra cross-block signal it appears to buy is maternal body habitus and image count -- acquisition conditions the encoder can read off the pixels. Putting this in the paper would mean claiming an image block that is partly a maternal-BMI proxy.
what_would_actually_work: a NON-orthogonal image summary with genuine within-block redundancy -- e.g. per-plane pooled embeddings (cerebral / abdominal / femur separately), or a small set of correlated radiomics families. Those would be a real block. PCs never can be.
caveats: PC1 is 71% of variance and correlates with nothing tabular (max |rho| ~0.1), consistent with the earlier finding that PC1 is the maturation axis
5 PCs chosen a priori at 89% variance; not swept
coverage 94% is higher than the lag's 90.4% because it needs only one image, not a datable visit
